description.text:
Defines a new type of subagent that can be invoked via invoke_subagent.

	Guidelines:
	* Use this tool if you need a specialized subagent for a task and none of the existing subagents are suitable.
	* Once the subagent is defined, it can be invoked repeatedly using invoke_subagent without calling this tool again.
	* The subagent will be defined with the specified name, description, system prompt, and tool groups.
	* By default, all subagents have read tools to research the codebase, and tools to communicate with other agents.

Invokes one or more subagents by name with a single tool call. Each subagent runs in the background with its own prompt and reports back when done.

Specify the Subagents array with one or more entries. Each entry defines a subagent to launch.

Communicate with subagents using the send_message tool. Examples of when to do this:
* To check on the status of a subagent.
* To send a running subagent further instructions.
* To send an idle subagent new instructions.

Guidelines:
* Each invoked subagent will be uniquely identified by its conversationID.
* Multiple subagents with the same type name can be invoked, with each subagent receiving a unique conversationID.
* If a task is a natural continuation of an existing subagent's work, send a message to that subagent with the task rather than invoking a new subagent to conserve resources.

description.text:
Edit Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) files at the cell level. This tool provides safe, structured operations on notebooks without risking JSON corruption.

Actions:
- 'list': List all cells with their index, type, and preview
- 'get': Get the full content of a specific cell
- 'get_with_outputs': Get cell content and outputs
- 'add': Add a new cell (code or markdown)
- 'update': Update the content of an existing cell
- 'delete': Delete a cell
- 'create': Create a new empty notebook

This tool should be used instead of regular file editing tools for .ipynb files.

Execute cells in a Colab/Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) file.

This tool executes the specified cells. Cell IDs are required for each cell to execute. Before using this tool, read the notebook and identify the cell IDs to execute. These are alpha numeric IDs that are part of the notebook's JSON structure. Do not use cell indexes. Only for use when editor or active document is detected.
Returns the execution status, count of executed cells, and cell outputs/error trace.

description.text:
Use this tool to ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions, with the goal of:
- Clarifying underspecified requirements
- Soliciting design feedback or user preferences
- Addressing ambiguous user intent
- Picking a solution from a list of options

When called, this tool renders an interactive modal containing the question, selectable options, a default write-in option, and Submit/Skip buttons. Execution is blocked until the user responds.

Guidance:
- When specifying files in the question, use github markdown links (e.g. [filename](file:///path/to/file)).
- Don't use this tool to ask trivial questions that can be answered with a single word (e.g. yes/no); output regular text to ask these questions.
- Don't include an 'other' option for write-in responses; one is always provided in the UI by default.
- Don't enumerate the options; they are enumerated by default.
- Don't include "Select all options that apply", or similar, in the question; the UI already includes this.
- If you recommend any options, list it first and prefix the option text with "(Recommended)".
- Format options as the user's direct response instead of describing your own actions.
- Set 'IsMultiSelect' to true to allow the user to select multiple options with checkboxes.

description.text:
Manage background tasks. Use this tool to list running tasks or interact with tasks that were sent to the background.

Actions:
- 'list': List all currently running background tasks
- 'kill': Cancel the task's execution
- 'status': Check the task's current status and log file location
- 'send_input': Send input to a running task

When mentioning tasks to the user, avoid using full task IDs and start timestamps; keep them human-readable.

Edit files using sed expressions. Executes GNU sed with the given Basic Regular Expressions sequentially on the target file in-place. SUBSTITUTIONS: 's/old/new/' replaces text. Add 'g' flag to replace all occurrences on each line.
DELETIONS: 'Nd' deletes line N. 'N,Md' deletes lines N through M.
APPENDS: Use the file_content argument with the r command to append lines — this avoids all escaping issues.Pass file_content: {"block1": "your code here..."} and use 'Nr block1' in expressions to append the content at the end of line N. The content is written verbatim with no escaping needed.
REPLACING: You should generally lean on deleting + appending with the r command to replace lines to avoid escape issues. For example to replace lines 20-35, use expressions: ["20,35d", "19r new"] with file_content: {"new": "\nint add(int a, int b) {\n  return a + b;\n}"}. You still have a/i/c commands but be careful with escaping characters, in general err on the side of caution and use d + r to do line replacements/insertions/appending. Note the \n at the beginning of new, since r APPENDS to the END of line 19 in the example.
RULES:
- Order line-addressed expressions from BOTTOM of file to TOP to prevent line number shifts.
- You should try plan all changes upfront in a single call, but sometimes it may be better to make sequential sed edits if they're overlapping.
- Do NOT make parallel sed_file calls to the same file.
- Only reference line numbers you have actually viewed.
- Newline in a/i/c/s requires escaping the backslashes with \\n.
- Use alternate delimiters when patterns contain '/': 's|old/path|new/path|g'.
- Case conversion modifiers (\U, \L, \u, \l) are NOT supported.

List the contents of a directory, i.e. all files and subdirectories that are children of the directory. Directory path must be an absolute path to a directory that exists. For each child in the directory, output will have: relative path to the directory, whether it is a directory or file, size in bytes if file, and number of children (recursive) if directory. description.text: Send standard input to a running command or to terminate a command. Use this to interact with REPLs, interactive commands, and long-running processes. The command must have been created by a previous run_command call. Use the command_status tool to check the status and output of the command after sending input.

Search for files and subdirectories within a specified directory using fd.
Search uses smart case and will ignore gitignored files by default.
Pattern and Excludes both use the glob format. If you are searching for Extensions, there is no need to specify both Pattern AND Extensions.
To avoid overwhelming output, the results are capped at 50 matches. Use the various arguments to filter the search scope as needed.
Results will include the type, size, modification time, and relative path.
